A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments on CSQA, GSM8K and AQuA, including stochastic decoding, parameter sensitivity and Qwen-3-32B results.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds TruthfulQA evaluation, additional model configurations, inference latency measurements and a baseline sample-count study.

M1.justification: The NCI and fDBD scoring procedures, analytical feature-mean proxy, top-k token selection and sequence averaging are unchanged. The decoded-token NCI variant already appeared in v1 Appendix E, now Appendix K. Additional model evaluations introduce no detector modification.

E1.justification: V2 retains CSQA, GSM8K and AQuA and adds open-ended TruthfulQA evaluation (Section 5.3, Table 6), substantially extending coverage beyond the original reasoning tasks. TriviaQA appears in the new limitations discussion without a documented evaluation protocol.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained detection experiments is unchanged. The new latency comparison in Table 4b introduces standard decoding without hallucination detection as an explicitly measured reference alongside Perplexity, NCI and fDBD. No new competing detector is introduced.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluations across Qwen3 sizes, a Llama base model, a Qwen MoE model and Mistral (Appendices B–E). New protocols include Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct judging for TruthfulQA, end-to-end latency measurement and SelfCheckGPT-NLI sample counts of five and ten. Retained experimental settings remain unchanged; the newly documented reasoning system prompts do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: Appendix F/Table 12 adds a sensitivity study testing whether increasing SelfCheckGPT-NLI's sample count from three to five or ten improves its relative performance on AQuA. Existing feature-mean comparisons, k-sensitivity tests, stochastic-decoding experiments and decoded-token analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five seeds for stochastic decoding and the decoded-token NCI comparison. V2 introduces no new uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting practice. Its sample-count study varies generated responses, not independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: All original tables retain their numerical results. Substantial additions include TruthfulQA AUROCs of 68.17 for NCI and 67.83 for fDBD, model comparisons in Tables 8–11, and latency of 32.54/32.71 ms per token versus 31.94 for standard decoding. Table 12 adds SelfCheckGPT-NLI scores of 65.51 and 66.52 with five and ten samples. These are new settings and measurements, not improvements to retained results.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3, Lemma 4.1 and their mathematical reasoning are unchanged. V1 Appendices C–D correspond to v2 Appendices I–J; terminology changes from embedding to feature do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged. The introduction retains the same central contribution: adapting geometric OOD detectors into training-free, single-sample hallucination detectors with strong reasoning-task performance. Additional evaluations support this contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific limitations concerning short-answer datasets such as TriviaQA and the restriction to two geometric scores. It also connects boundary geometry to prior noise-injection findings and explains applicability to MoE models through their dense language heads. These qualify and extend the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix G.3 newly supplies exact system prompts for all three reasoning datasets. Appendix H documents TruthfulQA few-shot examples, omission of the abstention example, and the judge model and exact judging prompt. Section 5.1 identifies A100 timing hardware. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the reasoning prompts are additional disclosure, not demonstrated changes to retained runs.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for TruthfulQA, TriviaQA and inference-time intervention, and explicitly relates fDBD to the previously cited noise-injection approach. The broader research positioning is retained. Updating publication details and consolidating fDBD's preprint/publication references do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: The original narrative and main section order largely remain intact. Changes include localized introduction edits, consistent feature terminology, updated publication front matter, additional experimental and implementation subsections, and appendix relabeling. The revision does not extensively rewrite the retained exposition.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a pipeline overview incorporating the geometric schematics, while the existing histograms are separately displayed in Figure 2. Table 4 gains accuracy and latency panels, and new tables display TruthfulQA, model-configuration and sample-count results. Table styling and appendix layout are also revised.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for generality and practical efficiency through broader model/task evaluation, measured latency and the sample-count check. Exact prompts and explicit applicability limits also improve reproducibility and interpretation. The additions have weaknesses: TruthfulQA judge accuracy is not validated, and Appendix D incorrectly calls fDBD strongest although Table 10 gives NCI 70.09 versus fDBD 69.60. These localized shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains over v1.
